knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit scaled-inequality encoding for a polyhedral active domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(C=\{y\in\mathbb R^n:Ay\le b\}\) is nonempty, then
\[
\operatorname{cl}\{(zy,z):z>0,\ y\in C\}=\{(x,z):z\ge0,\ Ax\le zb\}.
\]
For \(z>0\), this is equivalent to \(x/z\in C\); for \(z=0\), it is equivalent to \(x\in\operatorname{rec}C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral active domain is homogenized by scaling each inequality right-hand side by the activity variable; the zero-activity slice is its recession cone.

notation.meaning: Recession cone of the active domain.

Singleton Off-State Closure Criterion
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed perspective uses the recession function at zero activity; forcing the underlying variable to zero is exact exactly when no nonzero recession direction has finite cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The closed perspective satisfies \[\bar f^\pi(x,z)=\begin{cases}z f(x/z),&z>0,\\ f^\infty(x),&z=0,\\ +\infty,&z<0.\end{cases}\] Consequently, replacing its zero-activity branch by \(\delta_{\{0\}}\) is exact if and only if \(f^\infty(x)=+\infty\) for every \(x\neq0\). Any nonzero \(d\) with finite \(f^\infty(d)\) remains a valid finite-cost zero-activity direction.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp zero-activity closure boundary for disjunctive perspective formulations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero Cost Retains Every Recession Direction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal example showing that an imposed zero-variable off state can exclude valid closure points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\equiv0\) on \(\mathbb R^n\). Then \(f^\infty(d)=0\) for every \(d\), so \(\bar f^\pi(d,0)=0\) for every \(d\). A formulation imposing \(x=0\) whenever \(z=0\) therefore omits every point \((d,0,0)\) with \(d\ne0\) from the closed perspective epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the zero function, all directions survive at zero activity, so forcing the continuous variable to zero removes valid closure points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d\ne0\implies(d,0,0)\in\operatorname{epi}\bar f^\pi\), although it violates the rule \(z=0\Rightarrow x=0\).

notation.meaning: Closed perspective of the zero function

knowledge_statements.title: Zero Cost Retains Every Recession Direction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp recession criterion for whether an on–off perspective may force the continuous variable to zero at zero activity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proper lower-semicontinuous convex function \(f\), the closed perspective satisfies \[\bar f^\pi(x,z)=\begin{cases}zf(x/z),&z>0,\\ f^\infty(x),&z=0,\\ +\infty,&z<0.\end{cases}\] Consequently, the boundary rule \(\bar f^\pi(0,0)=0\) and \(\bar f^\pi(x,0)=+\infty\) for \(x\ne0\) is exact if and only if \(f^\infty(d)=+\infty\) for every \(d\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At zero activity the closed perspective is the recession function, so forcing the continuous variable to zero is exact precisely when no nonzero finite-cost recession direction exists.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar f^\pi(x,0)=f^\infty(x)\), and zero activity forces \(x=0\) exactly when \(f^\infty(d)=+\infty\) for all \(d\ne0\).

notation.meaning: Closed perspective of the convex cost

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Zero-Activity Closure Boundary
Disjunctive Closure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a perspective formulation when its zero-scale recession boundary is omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Defining \(z f(x/z)\) only for \(z>0\) and assigning a finite value at \(z=0\) solely when \(x=0\) need not produce a closed epigraph. For the proper closed convex function \(f(x)=x\) on \(\mathbb{R}\), one has \(z f(x/z)=x\) for every \(z>0\). Hence points \((x,z,t)\) with \(z\downarrow0\) and \(t\ge x\) converge to finite boundary points \((x,0,t)\) for arbitrary \(x\). The correct closure uses \(f^{\infty}(x)=x\), not an off boundary restricted to \(x=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A perspective can have finite nonzero states at zero scale. The linear-cost example shows that restricting the zero-scale boundary to the origin destroys closedness.
assumptions_latex: The naive boundary at \(z=0\) permits only \(x=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The naive perspective epigraph is not closed; its closed boundary satisfies \(t\ge f^{\infty}(x)=x\) at \(z=0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Separable Perspective Reformulations
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sum of independently activated convex costs is represented by separate closed-perspective epigraphs and a single constraint summing their epigraph variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(i\), define
\[
\bar f_i^\pi(x_i,z_i)=
\begin{cases}
z_i f_i(x_i/z_i),&z_i>0,\\
f_i^\infty(x_i),&z_i=0.
\end{cases}
\]
Then the separable perspective cost \(F(x,z)=\sum_{i=1}^m\bar f_i^\pi(x_i,z_i)\) is closed and convex, and its epigraph has the extended formulation
\[
F(x,z)\leq r\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists(r_i)_{i=1}^m:\ \bar f_i^\pi(x_i,z_i)\leq r_i\ \text{for all }i,\quad\sum_{i=1}^m r_i\leq r.
\]
Thus each separable term can be represented by its own perspective epigraph.
assumptions_latex: For \(i=1,\ldots,m\), \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
Each \(z_i\geq0\), and \(f_i^\infty\) denotes the recession function of \(f_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}\sum_i\bar f_i^\pi=\{(x,z,r):\exists r_i,\ r_i\geq\bar f_i^\pi(x_i,z_i),\ \sum_i r_i\leq r\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph reformulation for a finite sum of independently activated convex terms.

notation.meaning: Closed perspective of the ith separable term.
Epigraph allocation variable for the ith term.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A finite separable cost governed by one common activity variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f_i:\mathbb R^{n_i}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and set \(F(x_1,\ldots,x_m)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\). Then
\[
\bar F^\pi(x,z)=\sum_{i=1}^m\bar f_i^\pi(x_i,z)\qquad(z\ge0).
\]
At \(z=0\), this identity uses \(F^\infty(x)=\sum_i f_i^\infty(x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed perspective of a finite product-separable cost decomposes term by term even when all terms share one activity variable.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(I\) be finite. For each \(i\in I\), let \(f_i:\mathbb R^{n_i}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex with \(f_i(0)=0\), let \(z_i\in\{0,1\}\), and let \(x_i\in\mathbb R^{n_i}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite separable sums with one activation variable per separable block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the separable on–off cost \(\sum_{i\in I}G_i(x_i,z_i)\), the separable perspective reformulation is \[\sum_{i\in I}P_{f_i}(z_i,x_i),\qquad P_{f_i}(z_i,x_i)=\begin{cases}z_i f_i(x_i/z_i),&z_i>0,\\(\operatorname{rec}f_i)(x_i),&z_i=0,\\+\infty,&z_i<0.
\end{cases}\] In epigraph form one introduces \(t_i\) with \(t_i\ge P_{f_i}(z_i,x_i)\) and aggregates by \(t\ge\sum_i t_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separable perspective reformulation applies the perspective transformation independently to each convex block and its own activation indicator. The resulting relaxed cost is the sum of the block perspectives. An equivalent epigraph model introduces one cost variable per block and sums those variables. This blockwise construction preserves separability and exactly matches the original on–off costs when the indicators are binary.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The aggregate inequality \(t\ge\sum_iP_{f_i}(z_i,x_i)\) is equivalent to the existence of epigraph variables \(t_i\) satisfying the displayed block inequalities.
When \(z_i=1\), block \(i\) contributes \(f_i(x_i)\); when \(z_i=0\), it contributes its recession-closed off-state value.
special_cases_latex: For separable quadratics \(f_i(x_i)=q_i x_i^2\), the reformulated terms are \(q_i x_i^2/z_i\), represented by rotated second-order-cone inequalities.
immediate_consequences_latex: The relaxed objective is convex as a finite sum of closed perspectives.
Each block can retain its own bounds \(\ell_i z_i\le x_i\le u_i z_i\).
boundary_notes: A nonseparable function of several blocks cannot generally be strengthened by independently perspectivizing its coordinate terms.
Shared indicators require grouping all jointly activated variables into the corresponding perspective block.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conic Representability of a Perspective Epigraph
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex and let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a closed convex cone. Let \(P_f\) denote the closed perspective.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representability interface only; surrounding conic-programming theory and solution algorithms are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The perspective epigraph is \(K\)-representable if there exist matrices and vectors of compatible dimensions such that \[\operatorname{epi}P_f=\{(\xi,x,t):\exists y,\ A\xi+Bx+ct+Dy+e\in K\}.\] A perspective representability interface is an explicit equivalence between \(t\ge P_f(\xi,x)\) and such a lifted conic membership condition. If no auxiliary variable \(y\) is needed, the representation is direct.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perspective representability means that the epigraph of a closed perspective is the projection of an affine slice of a chosen closed convex cone. The interface consists of an exact equivalence between the perspective inequality and the lifted conic constraint. This definition classifies perspectives by representation type—such as second-order-cone or exponential-cone representability—without importing algorithms for solving the resulting conic program.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}P_f\) is the linear projection of \(\{(\xi,x,t,y):A\xi+Bx+ct+Dy+e\in K\}\).
Direct representability is the special case with no lifted variable.
special_cases_latex: For \(f(x)=x^2\), \(t\ge x^2/\xi\) with \(t,\xi\ge0\) is a rotated second-order-cone constraint.
Perspective mappings of second-order-cone representable sets remain second-order-cone representable under the homogenized construction described in the source.
immediate_consequences_latex: A finite sum of independently representable perspective epigraphs admits a product-cone lifted representation.
Representability provides an exact formulation class, not merely an approximation.
boundary_notes: The cone \(K\), lift, and affine map must be specified for an actual representation claim.
Closedness at \(\xi=0\) must be retained; a positive-scale formula alone is not a complete conic representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-over-Linear Perspectives
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed perspective of a squared norm is quadratic-over-linear for positive scale and is finite at zero scale exactly on the linear map's kernel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The lower-semicontinuous perspective of \(x\mapsto\|Ax\|_2^2\) is
\[
q_A(x,t)=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{\|Ax\|_2^2}{t},&t>0,\\
0,&t=0\text{ and }Ax=0,\\
+\infty,&t=0\text{ and }Ax\neq0,\\
+\infty,&t<0.
\end{cases}
\]
This function is convex and positively homogeneous in \((x,t)\). When \(A\) is injective, its finite zero-scale boundary consists only of \((x,t)=(0,0)\); for singular \(A\), every \(x\in\ker A\) has zero boundary value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_A(x,t)=\|Ax\|_2^2/t\) for \(t>0\), with the stated closed extension at \(t=0\), is convex and lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed perspective of a squared Euclidean norm under a linear map.

notation.meaning: Null space of the linear map.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the leaf, and the kernel-valued zero-scale boundary is mathematically consistent. A specific authoritative citation is missing.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Supremum-of-affine representation valid on the entire closed extended-real domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), the closed quadratic-over-linear perspective satisfies
\[
q_A(x,t)=\sup_{y\in\mathbb R^m}\{2\langle Ax,y\rangle-t\|y\|_2^2\}.
\]
For \(t>0\), the unique maximizer is \(y^*=Ax/t\). At \(t=0\), the supremum is zero when \(Ax=0\) and \(+\infty\) otherwise; for \(t<0\), it is \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic-over-linear is the supremum of affine functions indexed by a vector; at positive scale the maximizing vector is the scaled residual.

notation.meaning: Closed perspective of the squared Euclidean norm composed with A.
Unique maximizing vector at positive scale.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\) and define \(q(x)=x^\top Qx\) on \(\mathbb R^n\). Let \(Q^{1/2}\) be the positive-semidefinite square root.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional positive-semidefinite quadratic perspective with its closed zero-scale extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The quadratic-over-linear perspective of \(q\) is \[P_q(\xi,x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{x^\top Qx}{\xi},&\xi>0,\\0,&\xi=0\text{ and }Q^{1/2}x=0,\\+\infty,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}\] Its epigraph is \[\{(\xi,x,t):\xi\ge0,\ t\ge0,\ x^\top Qx\le\xi t\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive-semidefinite quadratic form \(q(x)=x^\top Qx\), the positive-scale perspective is the quadratic-over-linear function \(x^\top Qx/\xi\). Its closed zero-scale value is finite precisely on the nullspace of \(Q\), where it equals zero. The epigraph is characterized by the rotated quadratic inequality \(x^\top Qx\le\xi t\) together with \(\xi,t\ge0\), and is second-order-cone representable after factoring \(Q\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(Q=I\), the epigraph condition is \(\|x\|_2^2\le\xi t\).
The rotated-cone inequality is equivalent to \(\|(2Q^{1/2}x,\xi-t)\|_2\le\xi+t\).
special_cases_latex: In one dimension with \(Q=[1]\), \(P_q(\xi,x)=x^2/\xi\) for \(\xi>0\), and only \(x=0\) is finite at zero scale.
If \(Q\succ0\), the zero-scale effective domain is exactly \(\{0\}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The quadratic-over-linear function is closed and convex on its extended domain.
Its epigraph has a direct rotated second-order-cone representation.
boundary_notes: For singular \(Q\), nonzero nullspace vectors have zero cost at scale zero.
Indefinite \(Q\) is excluded because the base quadratic is not convex.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Define the closed entropy function \(h(s)=s\log s\) for \(s>0\), \(h(0)=0\), and \(h(s)=+\infty\) for \(s<0\). Define the exponential function \(e(r)=\exp r\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar closed perspectives and their finite separable sums; logarithms are natural.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The entropy perspective is the relative-entropy function \[P_h(t,s)=\begin{cases}s\log(s/t),&s>0,\ t>0,\\0,&s=0,\ t\ge0,\\+\infty,&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}\] with the standard endpoint convention. The exponential perspective is \[P_e(t,x)=\begin{cases}t\exp(x/t),&t>0,\\0,&t=0\text{ and }x\le0,\\+\infty,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}\] Finite sums \(\sum_iP_h(t_i,s_i)\) form the separable relative-entropy family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The perspective of negative entropy produces relative entropy: at positive arguments it is \(s\log(s/t)\), with the closed convention giving value zero when \(s=0\) and \(t\ge0\). The perspective of the exponential is \(t\exp(x/t)\) at positive scale; its closed zero-scale value is zero for nonpositive \(x\) and infinite for positive \(x\). Coordinatewise sums of entropy perspectives give standard separable divergence functions, including Kullback–Leibler-type expressions on the positive orthant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[P_h(t,s)=s\log(s/t)\quad(s,t>0),\qquad P_e(t,x)=t e^{x/t}\quad(t>0),\] with zero-scale values determined by the displayed recession branches.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For positive vectors \(s,t\), \(\sum_iP_h(t_i,s_i)=\sum_i s_i\log(s_i/t_i)\).
The inequality \(y\ge P_e(t,x)\) is the homogeneous exponential-epigraph relation \(y\ge t\exp(x/t)\).
special_cases_latex: On probability vectors, the separable entropy perspective yields the Kullback–Leibler divergence.
Taking a general scalar convex generator \(\phi\) gives the Csiszár family \(\sum_i t_i\phi(s_i/t_i)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Both displayed closed perspectives are proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions.
Their separable sums remain convex on the corresponding product domain.
boundary_notes: The relative-entropy expression has extended-real endpoint conventions; the quotient formula alone is not defined when \(s=0\) or \(t=0\).
The source states the positive-domain Kullback–Leibler formula explicitly; the endpoint values here use the recession-closed perspective convention.

Closed perspective of the exponential function.

knowledge_statements.title: Exponential Perspectives
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exponential perspective is scale times an exponential at positive scale; its closed zero-scale boundary is finite precisely in nonpositive directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The closed perspective of the exponential function is
\[
\bar f^\pi(u,v)=
\begin{cases}
v\exp(u/v),&v>0,\\
0,&v=0\text{ and }u\leq0,\\
+\infty,&v=0\text{ and }u>0,\\
+\infty,&v<0.
\end{cases}
\]
The values at \(v=0\) equal the recession function of \(f\): nonpositive directions have zero recession cost, whereas positive directions have infinite recession cost. Consequently, \(\bar f^\pi\) is convex, lower semicontinuous, and positively homogeneous on \(\mathbb{R}^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar f^\pi(u,v)=v e^{u/v}\) for \(v>0\), with recession boundary \(0\) when \(v=0,u\leq0\) and \(+\infty\) otherwise.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed scalar exponential perspective, including all zero-scale boundary values.

notation.meaning: Closed perspective of the exponential function.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits exponential perspectives, and the stated recession boundary is consistent. No source reference or locator is provided.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Interior Differential Geometry of the Exponential Perspective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gradient and curvature of the scalar exponential perspective at positive scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\psi(u,v)=v e^{u/v}\) with \(v>0\), writing \(r=u/v\),
\[
\nabla\psi(u,v)=e^r\begin{pmatrix}1\\1-r\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\nabla^2\psi(u,v)=\frac{e^r}{v}
\begin{pmatrix}1\\-r\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}1&-r\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Thus \(\nabla^2\psi(u,v)\) is positive semidefinite of rank one and has nullspace \(\operatorname{span}\{(u,v)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exponential perspective has rank-one positive curvature transverse to scaling rays and zero curvature along those rays.

notation.meaning: Exponential perspective restricted to positive scale.

knowledge_statements.title: Interior Differential Geometry of the Exponential Perspective
Entropy Perspectives
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The entropy perspective is relative entropy between a nonnegative mass and its scale; at zero scale it is finite only when the mass also vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The closed perspective of scalar negative entropy is
\[
\bar h^\pi(x,t)=
\begin{cases}
x\log(x/t),&x>0\text{ and }t>0,\\
0,&x=0\text{ and }t\geq0,\\
+\infty,&x>0\text{ and }t=0,\\
+\infty,&x<0\text{ or }t<0.
\end{cases}
\]
Here the value at \(x=0,t>0\) is understood by continuity. The function is convex, lower semicontinuous, and positively homogeneous. In particular, superlinear growth of \(h\) makes every nonzero nonnegative direction infinitely costly at zero scale.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar h^\pi(x,t)=x\log(x/t)\) for \(x\geq0,t>0\), and its only finite point with \(t=0\) is \((0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed perspective of scalar negative entropy with the convention \(0\log0=0\).

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits entropy perspectives, and the boundary conventions are internally consistent. The record lacks an inspectable authoritative citation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Interior Differential Geometry of the Entropy Perspective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gradient and curvature of scalar relative entropy on its positive domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\phi(x,t)=x\log(x/t)\) on \(x>0,t>0\),
\[
\nabla\phi(x,t)=\begin{pmatrix}\log(x/t)+1\\-x/t\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\nabla^2\phi(x,t)=\frac1x
\begin{pmatrix}1\\-x/t\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}1&-x/t\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Thus \(\nabla^2\phi(x,t)\) is positive semidefinite of rank one and has nullspace \(\operatorname{span}\{(x,t)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The entropy perspective has rank-one positive curvature transverse to scaling rays and zero curvature along each scaling ray.
knowledge_statements.title: Interior Differential Geometry of the Entropy Perspective
Dual Exponential Cone
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the fixed primal coordinate order, the dual exponential cone has an exponential branch with negative first coordinate and a nonnegative boundary branch at zero first coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[
K_{\exp}=\operatorname{cl}\{(u,v,w):v>0,\ v\exp(u/v)\leq w\},
\]
its Euclidean dual cone is
\[
K_{\exp}^*=\{(a,b,c):a<0,\ c\geq-a\exp(b/a-1)\}\cup\{(0,b,c):b\geq0,\ c\geq0\}.
\]
Thus dual feasibility can be checked either by the exponential inequality in the negative-first-coordinate branch or by the nonnegative boundary orthant when the first coordinate vanishes.
assumptions_latex: The dual cone is taken with respect to the standard Euclidean pairing.
The primal coordinate convention is \(K_{\exp}=\operatorname{cl}\{(u,v,w):v>0,\ v\exp(u/v)\leq w\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual exponential cone under exactly the coordinate convention used by the primal representability record.

notation.meaning: Dual of the closed exponential cone under the Euclidean pairing.

knowledge_statements.title: Entropy-Perspective Exponential-Cone Representation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar entropy-perspective epigraph is one exponential-cone constraint after negating the epigraph coordinate and permuting the entropy mass and scale into the cone's second and third coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the convention
\[
K_{\exp}=\operatorname{cl}\{(u,v,w):v>0,\ v\exp(u/v)\leq w\},
\]
the closed entropy-perspective epigraph satisfies
\[
r\geq\bar h^\pi(x,t)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad(-r,x,t)\in K_{\exp}.
\]
This equivalence includes \(x=0,t\geq0,r\geq0\) and excludes nonzero mass at zero scale.
assumptions_latex: The closed exponential cone uses \(K_{\exp}=\operatorname{cl}\{(u,v,w):v>0,\ v\exp(u/v)\leq w\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact exponential-cone representation of the scalar entropy-perspective epigraph under the fixed coordinate convention.

notation.meaning: Closed exponential cone in the fixed coordinate order.
Closed perspective of scalar negative entropy.

assumptions_latex: The closed exponential cone uses the coordinate convention \(K_{\exp}=\operatorname{cl}\{(u,v,w):v>0,\ v e^{u/v}\leq w\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w\geq\bar f^\pi(u,v)\) if and only if \((u,v,w)\in K_{\exp}\).

notation.meaning: Closed perspective of the scalar exponential.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact conic epigraph representation under an explicitly fixed exponential-cone coordinate order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
K_{\exp}=\operatorname{cl}\{(u,v,w)\in\mathbb{R}^3:v>0,\ v\exp(u/v)\leq w\}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
K_{\exp}=\{(u,v,w):v>0,\ v\exp(u/v)\leq w\}\cup\{(u,0,w):u\leq0,\ w\geq0\}.
\]
For the closed exponential perspective \(\bar f^\pi\), the epigraph equivalence is
\[
w\geq\bar f^\pi(u,v)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad(u,v,w)\in K_{\exp}.
\]
Thus one exponential-cone membership constraint represents both the positive-scale exponential inequality and its lower-semicontinuous zero-scale boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exponential-perspective epigraph is exactly one closed exponential-cone constraint, including the nonpositive zero-scale boundary ray.
knowledge_statements.title: Exponential-Cone Representability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind is correct for this leaf, and the explicitly stated coordinate convention makes the equivalence coherent. The cone convention and closure formula require a cited source with a precise locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Entropy-Domain Boundary Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At zero scale, the exponential perspective is finite along a nonpositive ray, while the negative-entropy perspective is finite only at zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At zero scale, the two closed perspectives have different finite domains:
\[
\bar f^\pi(u,0)=
\begin{cases}0,&u\leq0,\\+\infty,&u>0,
\end{cases}
\qquad
\bar h^\pi(x,0)=
\begin{cases}0,&x=0,\\+\infty,&x\neq0.
\end{cases}
\]
The exponential admits a nonpositive recession ray because its values tend to zero along negative directions. Negative entropy is superlinear on its nonnegative domain, so its closed perspective admits no nonzero finite recession direction. These boundary assignments are required for lower semicontinuity and cannot be inferred by substituting a zero denominator into the positive-scale formulas.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar f^\pi(u,0)<+\infty\) exactly when \(u\leq0\), whereas \(\bar h^\pi(x,0)<+\infty\) exactly when \(x=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of zero-scale domains for conjugate exponential and negative-entropy perspectives.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The property kind appropriately records the contrasting boundary regimes, and the two formulas are consistent with the neighboring perspective records. No supporting citation is attached.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Supporting-hyperplane behavior at the finite boundary of the scalar entropy perspective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\phi\) be the closed perspective of \(h(x)=x\log x\) on \(x\ge0\). Then
\[
\partial\phi(0,0)=\{(a,b)\in\mathbb R^2:b+e^{a-1}\le0\},
\qquad
\partial\phi(0,t)=\varnothing\quad(t>0).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed entropy perspective has an entire supporting set at the zero-scale origin but no finite subgradient at zero mass and positive scale.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\) is the closed perspective of \(h(x)=x\log x\) on \(x\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Convex subdifferential of the entropy perspective.

knowledge_statements.title: Entropy-Perspective Boundary Subgradients

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Supporting sets along the finite zero-scale ray of the scalar exponential perspective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\psi\) be the closed perspective of \(f(u)=e^u\), and define
\[
K=\{(a,b)\in\mathbb R^2:a\ge0,\ b+a\log a-a\le0\},
\]
with \(0\log0=0\). Then
\[
\partial\psi(0,0)=K,
\qquad
\partial\psi(u,0)=\{(0,b):b\le0\}\quad(u<0).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the endpoint of its zero-scale ray the exponential perspective has the full entropy-defined supporting set, while interior points of the ray retain only nonpositive vertical supports.

notation.meaning: Dual supporting set determined by the conjugate of the exponential.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed Perspective of a Powered Norm
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\neq\{0\}\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(p\in(1,+\infty)\), and let \(\varphi(x)=\|x\|^p\). Values lie in \(( -\infty,+\infty]\), and the scale variable is \(\xi\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This finite- or infinite-dimensional Hilbert-space entry covers the closed convex perspective of a powered norm. It does not assert representability by any particular finite-dimensional cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The power-gauge perspective associated with \(\varphi=\|\cdot\|^p\) is the function \[G_p(\xi,x)=\begin{cases}\|x\|^p/\xi^{p-1},&\xi>0,\\0,&(\xi,x)=(0,0),\\+\infty,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}\] Its effective domain is \(\{(\xi,x):\xi>0\}\cup\{(0,0)\}\). This is the lower-semicontinuous convex extension of the positive-scale expression \(\xi\varphi(x/\xi)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonzero real Hilbert space and an exponent strictly larger than one, the power-gauge perspective equals the norm of x to power p divided by the scale to power p minus one when the scale is positive. It is zero at the zero-scale origin and positive infinity everywhere else. Its domain therefore consists of all positive scales together with the origin, and it is the lower-semicontinuous convex extension of the ordinary positive-scale perspective.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(\xi>0\), \(G_p(\xi,x)=\xi\varphi(x/\xi)\), while at \(\xi=0\) its value is \((\operatorname{rec}\varphi)(x)=\iota_{\{0\}}(x)\).
Its epigraph is \[\operatorname{epi}G_p=\operatorname{cl}\{(\xi,\xi u,\xi r):\xi>0,\ r\geq\|u\|^p\}.\]
special_cases_latex: For \(p=2\), \(G_2(\xi,x)=\|x\|^2/\xi\) on \(\xi>0\), giving the quadratic-over-linear perspective with its closed value at the origin.
immediate_consequences_latex: Positive homogeneity holds: \(G_p(\lambda\xi,\lambda x)=\lambda G_p(\xi,x)\) for every \(\lambda>0\).
Every sublevel set \(\{(\xi,x):G_p(\xi,x)\leq a\}\) is closed and convex.
boundary_notes: The endpoint \(p=1\) has a different zero-scale recession value and is not included.
Continuity relative to the effective domain can fail at \((0,0)\), even though the function is lower semicontinuous on the ambient space.
Replacing the norm by a noncoercive gauge can enlarge the finite zero-scale domain and requires its recession function.

notation.meaning: proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions on the Hilbert space
recession function of the convex function
indicator equal to zero on C and positive infinity off C

knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Power Perspective Variants
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonnegative-domain power has only the origin finite at zero scale, while the positive-part power retains the whole nonpositive zero-cost recession ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the nonnegative-domain power \(g(x)=x^p\) on \(x\geq0\), extended by \(+\infty\) on \(x<0\),
\[
\bar g^\pi(x,t)=
\begin{cases}
x^p t^{1-p},&t>0,\ x\geq0,\\
0,&t=0,\ x=0,\\
+\infty,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
For the positive-part power \(q(x)=(\max\{x,0\})^p\),
\[
\bar q^\pi(x,t)=
\begin{cases}(\max\{x,0\})^p t^{1-p},&t>0,\\
0,&t=0,\ x\leq0,\\
+\infty,&t=0,\ x>0,\\
+\infty,&t<0.
\end{cases}
\]
Thus extending a one-sided power by infinity or by a flat zero branch produces different recession domains and different closed perspective boundaries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar g^\pi\) is finite at zero scale only at \(x=0\), whereas \(\bar q^\pi(x,0)=0\) for every \(x\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two standard one-sided scalar convex power conventions and their distinct closed zero-scale branches.

notation.meaning: Closed perspective of the nonnegative-domain power.
Closed perspective of the positive-part power.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Domain of a Scalar Power Perspective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel conjugate and contact certificate for the closed scalar power perspective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p>1\), \(q=p/(p-1)\), and \(c_p=(p-1)p^{-q}\). For \(f(x)=|x|^p\), \(f^*(y)=c_p|y|^q\). If \(P=\bar f^\pi\), then
\[
P^*(y,s)=\delta_{D_p}(y,s),\qquad D_p=\{(y,s):s+c_p|y|^q\le0\}.
\]
For \(t>0\), equality in \(xy+ts\le P(x,t)\) on \(s=-c_p|y|^q\) holds exactly when
\[
y=p\,\operatorname{sgn}(x/t)|x/t|^{p-1}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate of a scalar power perspective is the indicator of a hypograph determined by the conjugate exponent, and equality gives an explicit contact certificate.
assumptions_latex: P\text{ is the closed perspective of }f(x)=|x|^p.

notation.meaning: Effective dual domain of the power perspective.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Domain of a Scalar Power Perspective
Power Perspectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed perspective of a scalar power function for exponent strictly greater than one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(p>1\) and let \(f(x)=|x|^p/p\) on \(\mathbb{R}\). Its closed perspective is
\[P_p(x,t)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{|x|^p}{p\,t^{p-1}},&t>0,\\0,&(x,t)=(0,0),\\+\infty,&t=0,\ x\ne0,\\+\infty,&t<0.\end{cases}\]
The function \(P_p\) is proper, closed, convex, and positively homogeneous of degree one in \((x,t)\). Consequently, its epigraph is a closed convex cone and supplies a homogeneous representation of the power-over-scale expression.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The perspective of the p-power is power divided by scale to degree p−1, with only the origin finite at zero scale.

knowledge_statements.title: Gauge Perspectives
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Because a gauge is already positively homogeneous, taking its closed perspective leaves its value unchanged for every nonnegative scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(t>0\), positive homogeneity gives
\[
t\gamma(x/t)=\gamma(x).
\]
Moreover, a closed convex gauge satisfies \(\gamma^\infty=\gamma\). Hence its closed perspective is
\[
\bar\gamma^\pi(x,t)=
\begin{cases}
\gamma(x),&t\geq0,\\
+\infty,&t<0.
\end{cases}
\]
Thus perspective scaling introduces no new nonlinear dependence on the nonnegative scale variable. Equivalently, the epigraph condition \(r\geq\bar\gamma^\pi(x,t)\) is simply \(r\geq\gamma(x)\) together with \(t\geq0\).
assumptions_latex: \(\gamma:\mathbb{R}^n\to[0,+\infty]\) is a closed convex gauge, so \(\gamma(\lambda x)=\lambda\gamma(x)\) for \(\lambda\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degeneracy of perspective scaling for closed positively homogeneous convex functions.

notation.meaning: Unit sublevel set of the gauge.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the scale-invariance phenomenon for gauge perspectives, and the statement is internally consistent for a closed convex gauge. No inspectable citation is supplied.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel conjugate of the scale-invariant closed gauge perspective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\gamma\) be a proper closed convex gauge and
\[
H(x,t)=\gamma(x)+\delta_{\mathbb R_+}(t).
\]
For \(B_{\gamma^\circ}=\{y:\langle y,x\rangle\le\gamma(x)\ \forall x\}\),
\[
H^*(y,s)=\delta_{B_{\gamma^\circ}}(y)+\delta_{\mathbb R_-}(s).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conjugate of a closed gauge perspective is the indicator of the polar-gauge unit ball times the nonpositive scale-dual half-line.
assumptions_latex: \gamma\text{ is a proper closed convex gauge}.

notation.meaning: Polar-gauge unit ball, equivalently the dual set dominated by the gauge.

knowledge_statements.title: Conjugate of a Gauge Perspective
Dual Power Cone
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual power cone is a coordinate scaling of the power cone, with scaling determined by its exponent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<\alpha<1\), let \[K_\alpha=\{(r,t,x):r\geq0,\ t\geq0,\ |x|\leq r^\alpha t^{1-\alpha}\}.\] Under the Euclidean pairing, \[K_\alpha^*=\left\{(u,v,w):u\geq0,\ v\geq0,\ |w|\leq\left(\frac{u}{\alpha}\right)^\alpha\left(\frac{v}{1-\alpha}\right)^{1-\alpha}\right\}=\operatorname{diag}(\alpha,1-\alpha,1)K_\alpha.\]
assumptions_latex: Duality uses the Euclidean pairing and coordinates \((r,t,x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual cone under the power-cone coordinate convention fixed by the seed.

notation.meaning: Nonnegative dual of the power cone.

assumptions_latex: The power cone is \(K_\alpha=\{(r,t,x):r\geq0,\ t\geq0,\ |x|\leq r^\alpha t^{1-\alpha}\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r\geq\bar f^\pi(x,t)\) if and only if \((r,t,x)\in K_{1/p}\), where \(f(x)=|x|^p\).

notation.meaning: Three-dimensional power cone with exponent alpha.
Closed perspective of the scalar p-power.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact scalar power-perspective epigraph representation under an explicit power-cone convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=|x|^p\), \(p>1\), and \(\alpha=1/p\). For \(t>0\),
\[
r\geq |x|^p t^{1-p}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
|x|\leq r^{1/p}t^{1-1/p}.
\]
After taking closures, the equivalence remains valid at \(t=0\). Therefore
\[
r\geq\bar f^\pi(x,t)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
(r,t,x)\in K_{1/p},
\]
where
\[
K_{1/p}=\{(r,t,x):r\geq0,\ t\geq0,\ |x|\leq r^{1/p}t^{1-1/p}\}.
\]
The cone boundary enforces \(x=0\) whenever \(t=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The epigraph of a scalar p-power perspective is exactly a three-dimensional power cone with exponent one over p.
knowledge_statements.title: Power-Cone Representability

knowledge_statements.title: Nondefinite Gauge Zero-Height Slice
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nondefinite gauge, the homogeneous power-gauge lift has zero-height rays over every zero-gauge direction; the origin-only zero slice is equivalent to definiteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(N=\{x\in V:\gamma(x)=0\}\) and \(f=\gamma^p\). Then \(f^\infty=\delta_N\), and consequently
\[
\operatorname{epi}\bar f^\pi=\{(x,t,r):t>0,\ \gamma(x)^p\leq r t^{p-1}\}\cup\{(x,0,r):x\in N,\ r\geq0\}.
\]
Thus the zero-height slice reduces to \(\{(0,0,r):r\geq0\}\) exactly when \(\gamma\) is definite.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp extension of the homogeneous power-gauge lift when the gauge has nontrivial zero directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Homogeneous Gauge Lifts
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed perspective epigraph of a positive power of a definite gauge is the conic hull of its unit-scale epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[K_{\gamma,p}=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{cone}\bigl\{(u,1,s)\in V\times\mathbb R^2:\gamma(u)^p\le s\bigr\}.\] Then \[K_{\gamma,p}=\bigl\{(x,t,r):t>0,\ \gamma(x)^p\le r t^{p-1}\bigr\}\cup\bigl\{(0,0,r):r\ge0\bigr\}.\] Thus membership is invariant under common nonnegative scaling of \((x,t,r)\), and its section at \(t=1\) is the epigraph of \(\gamma^p\).
assumptions_latex: \(\gamma:V\to[0,+\infty]\) is a closed convex gauge with \(\gamma(x)=0\) only for \(x=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K_{\gamma,p}\) is a closed convex cone representing the closed perspective of \(\gamma^p\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional conic lift of a power-gauge perspective.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp extension of the accepted definite-gauge lift to finite gauges with nontrivial zero directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\gamma:V\to[0,+\infty)\) be a finite closed convex gauge, \(p>1\), and \(Z=\{z:\gamma(z)=0\}\). The closed perspective epigraph of \(\gamma^p\) is
\[
\{(x,t,r):t>0,\ \gamma(x)^p\le r t^{p-1}\}\cup\{(z,0,r):z\in Z,\ r\ge0\}.
\]
Its zero-scale face reduces to \(\{(0,0,r):r\ge0\}\) exactly when \(\gamma\) is definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without definiteness, every zero-gauge direction survives on the lift's zero-scale face; definiteness is exactly what collapses that face to the vertical ray.
assumptions_latex: \gamma:V\to[0,+\infty)\text{ is a finite closed convex gauge}.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\) be a real Hilbert space and \(\varphi\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\). Define the open perspective \(F\) by \(F(\xi,x)=\xi\varphi(x/\xi)\) for \(\xi>0\) and \(+\infty\) otherwise, and let \(G\) denote its lower-semicontinuous convex envelope.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The boundary is defined epigraphically and records exactly what positive-scale homogenization omits. It concerns closure at scale zero, not numerical instability or cone-specific modeling syntax.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The perspective failure boundary of \(\varphi\) is \[\mathcal B_\varphi:=\operatorname{epi}G\setminus\operatorname{epi}F.\] Since \[G(\xi,x)=\begin{cases}\xi\varphi(x/\xi),&\xi>0,\\(\operatorname{rec}\varphi)(x),&\xi=0,\\+\infty,&\xi<0,\end{cases}\] the boundary has the explicit form \[\mathcal B_\varphi=\{(0,x,r):r\in\mathbb R,\ r\geq(\operatorname{rec}\varphi)(x)\}.\] Thus it is precisely the finite-height zero-scale epigraph contributed by recession geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start with the perspective defined only at positive scales and compare its epigraph with the epigraph of its lower-semicontinuous convex envelope. The perspective failure boundary is the set difference between those epigraphs. It consists exactly of zero-scale triples whose height is at least the recession value of the underlying function. Negative scales add no finite points, while positive scales already belong to the original perspective epigraph.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The failure boundary is the closure defect \(\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{epi}F)\setminus\operatorname{epi}F\).
A zero-scale point \((0,x,r)\) belongs to the closed homogenized model exactly when \((x,r)\in\operatorname{epi}(\operatorname{rec}\varphi)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\varphi(x)=\|x\|^p\) with \(p>1\), then \(\operatorname{rec}\varphi=\iota_{\{0\}}\), so \(\mathcal B_\varphi=\{(0,0,r):r\geq0\}\).
If \(\varphi\) is sublinear, then \(\operatorname{rec}\varphi=\varphi\), and the entire zero-scale copy \(\{0\}\times\operatorname{epi}\varphi\) is required.
immediate_consequences_latex: The positive-scale model is closed exactly when \(\mathcal B_\varphi\) is empty; for a proper perspective defined as above, the closure normally contributes at least the zero-scale origin.
Any formulation omitting \(\mathcal B_\varphi\) fails to represent the closed perspective epigraph.
boundary_notes: This definition does not identify points lost through a later projection onto other variables.
A finite value at \(\xi<0\) is outside the closed perspective convention.
The set difference is epigraphical; it should not be confused with the topological boundary of \(\operatorname{epi}G\).

knowledge_statements.title: Naive Zero-Scale Extensions
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the quadratic, declaring every zero-scale point finite destroys convexity; only the recession-compatible zero-scale boundary is valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(P_0(x,t)=x^2/t\) for \(t>0\), and naively set \(P_0(x,0)=0\) for every \(x\). Although \(P_0(1,0)=P_0(0,1)=0\), one has \[P_0\bigl((1,0)/2+(0,1)/2\bigr)=P_0(1/2,1/2)=1/2>0.\] Hence the convexity inequality fails. The closed perspective instead assigns \(+\infty\) at \((x,0)\) whenever \(x\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The naive zero-scale extension is not convex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure caused by assigning finite values indiscriminately at zero scale.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space and let \(\varphi:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex. Its positive-scale perspective is \(P_+(t,x)=t\varphi(x/t)\) for \(t>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This entry formalizes one common naive convention: append only the zero-scale origin without consulting the recession function. It is a diagnostic object, not the canonical closed perspective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The naive origin-only zero-scale extension of \(P_+\) is \[P_{\mathrm n}(t,x)=\begin{cases}t\varphi(x/t),&t>0,\\0,&(t,x)=(0,0),\\+\infty,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}\] It is called zero-scale exact for \(\varphi\) when \[P_{\mathrm n}(0,x)=(\operatorname{rec}\varphi)(x)\quad\text{for every }x\in X,\] equivalently when \(\operatorname{rec}\varphi=\iota_{\{0\}}\). Otherwise its zero-scale slice omits every \(x\neq0\) having finite recession value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The naive origin-only extension keeps the usual perspective at positive scales, assigns value zero only when both scale and vector are zero, and assigns positive infinity everywhere else. It agrees with the correct recession-based zero-scale extension exactly when the recession function is the indicator of the origin. If the underlying function has any nonzero direction with finite recession value, the naive extension excludes legitimate zero-scale points.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The zero-scale domain of \(P_{\mathrm n}\) is \(\{0\}\), whereas the zero-scale domain of the closed perspective is \(\operatorname{dom}(\operatorname{rec}\varphi)\).
Zero-scale exactness is equivalent to \(\operatorname{dom}(\operatorname{rec}\varphi)=\{0\}\) together with \((\operatorname{rec}\varphi)(0)=0\).
special_cases_latex: For \(\varphi(x)=\|x\|^p\) with \(p>1\), the origin-only extension is zero-scale exact.
For a norm or any finite sublinear function, the origin-only extension is not zero-scale exact because \(\operatorname{rec}\varphi=\varphi\) is finite beyond the origin.
immediate_consequences_latex: When zero-scale exactness fails, \(\operatorname{epi}P_{\mathrm n}\) is strictly smaller than the epigraph of the closed perspective.
Substituting \(t=0\) directly into \(t\varphi(x/t)\) is not a definition; an explicit zero-scale rule is necessary.
boundary_notes: The convention assigning \(+\infty\) at every \(t=0\), including \((0,0)\), is a different naive extension.
No inspected source supplied this terminology or this exact diagnostic definition.

The formula is mathematically precise but the node terminology requires source confirmation.

Positive-Scale Perspective Epigraphs Omit the Origin
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The positive-scale perspective epigraph of every proper function is nonclosed because it omits the origin approached along each scaled epigraph ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(u\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and every real \(a\geq f(u)\), the points \((\tau u,\tau,\tau a)\) belong to \(E_+(f)\) for \(\tau>0\) and converge to \((0,0,0)\) as \(\tau\downarrow0\). Since \(E_+(f)\) excludes scale zero, it is not closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E_+(f)\text{ is not closed, and }(0,0,0)\in\operatorname{cl}E_+(f)\setminus E_+(f).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic closure failure caused solely by excluding the zero-scale slice.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonclosed Perspective Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting the quadratic perspective epigraph to positive scales omits its limiting zero-scale ray and produces a nonclosed convex model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The set \[E_+=\bigl\{(x,t,r)\in\mathbb R^3:t>0,\ x^2/t\le r\bigr\}\] is convex, but it is not closed. Indeed, \((0,1/n,0)\in E_+\) for every positive integer \(n\), while \((0,1/n,0)\to(0,0,0)\notin E_+\). Its closure adds the zero-scale ray \(\{(0,0,r):r\ge0\}\), which is required by the closed perspective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The positive-scale perspective epigraph is convex but not closed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of closedness when the zero-scale boundary is omitted.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex, and set \(E_+=\{(x,t,r):t>0,\ r\ge t f(x/t)\}\). Then \(E_+\) is convex but not closed, and \((0,0,0)\in\operatorname{cl}E_+\setminus E_+\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\) be a real Hilbert space and \(\varphi\in\Gamma_0(\mathcal H)\). Set \(C=\{1\}\times\operatorname{epi}\varphi\subset\mathbb R\times\mathcal H\times\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The model is the raw positive-scale homogenization. Nonclosedness is an epigraph property in the ambient product topology; the entry does not claim that every subsequent projection is nonclosed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The nonclosed perspective model generated by \(\varphi\) is \[F(\xi,x)=\begin{cases}\xi\varphi(x/\xi),&\xi>0,\\+\infty,&\xi\leq0.
\end{cases}\] Its epigraph is \(\operatorname{epi}F=\operatorname{cone}C\). It is called nonclosed when \[\operatorname{epi}F\neq\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{epi}F),\] equivalently when \(F\) is not lower semicontinuous. Its closed completion is obtained by assigning \((\operatorname{rec}\varphi)(x)\) at \(\xi=0\) and \(+\infty\) at \(\xi<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The raw perspective model uses the ordinary perspective formula only for positive scale and assigns positive infinity for nonpositive scale. Its epigraph is the conic hull of the unit-scale epigraph. The model is nonclosed when that conic hull is not closed, or equivalently when the extended-real function is not lower semicontinuous. Closing the model adds the recession-function slice at zero scale.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Nonclosedness means that there are \((\xi_k,x_k,r_k)\in\operatorname{epi}F\) converging to a point outside \(\operatorname{epi}F\).

The closed completion is \[\overline F(\xi,x)=\begin{cases}\xi\varphi(x/\xi),&\xi>0,\\(\operatorname{rec}\varphi)(x),&\xi=0,\\+\infty,&\xi<0.
\end{cases}\]
special_cases_latex: For \(\varphi(x)=\|x\|^p\), \(p>1\), the missing finite zero-scale point is the origin, with all epigraph heights above zero.
For sublinear \(\varphi\), the closed completion has the full slice \(\overline F(0,x)=\varphi(x)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A minimization model using \(F\) may have the same infimum as its completion while failing to attain a limiting zero-scale solution.
Replacing \(F\) by its closed completion preserves every positive-scale value.
boundary_notes: Convexity alone does not imply closedness.
The restriction of \(F\) to \(\xi>0\) can be continuous even though the ambient extended-real function is nonclosed.
This definition concerns the perspective before any additional affine image or elimination.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive-Scale Perspective Epigraphs Are Not Closed
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic closure failure caused solely by excluding the zero-scale slice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, and define \[E_+(f):=\{(x,t,r):t>0,\ r\ge t f(x/t)\}.\] Then \(E_+(f)\) is not closed. Indeed, for any \(u\in\operatorname{dom}f\) and \(a\ge f(u)\), \((tu,t,ta)\in E_+(f)\) for every \(t>0\), while \((tu,t,ta)\to(0,0,0)\notin E_+(f)\) as \(t\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every proper function, excluding zero scale makes the positive-scale perspective epigraph nonclosed because scaled epigraph points converge to the omitted origin.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Scale Perspective Epigraphs Are Not Closed
Missing Homogenized Domain Constraints
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Homogenizing the indicator of an interval requires all inequalities defining its scaled domain; omitting one admits invalid zero-scale points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The closed perspective epigraph of \(f\) is \[E=\bigl\{(x,t,r)\in\mathbb R^3:0\le x\le t,\ t\ge0,\ r\ge0\bigr\}.\] Retaining only \(x\le t\) and \(r\ge0\) admits, for example, \((-1,0,0)\), which does not belong to \(E\). Thus homogenization must preserve every domain inequality, including the scale constraint and the homogenized lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dropping homogenized domain inequalities strictly enlarges the perspective epigraph.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Indicator example exposing indispensable homogenized domain constraints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-by-constraint audit of the homogenized domain for the interval indicator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f=\delta_{[0,1]}\), the homogenized domain is \(K=\{(x,t):0\le x\le t\}\). Omitting \(x\ge0\) admits \((-1,1)\), and omitting \(x\le t\) admits \((2,1)\). The separate inequality \(t\ge0\) is redundant once both inequalities are retained, since \(0\le x\le t\) implies \(t\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Both scaled interval bounds are indispensable, while a separate nonnegative-scale inequality is redundant for this particular representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequalities \(x\ge0\) and \(x\le t\) are individually necessary, whereas \(t\ge0\) is implied by them.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\varphi:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex on a finite-dimensional space. Let \(G\) be its closed perspective and \(E=\operatorname{epi}G\subset\mathbb R\times X\times\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition diagnoses set-theoretic omission of scale-domain or recession-slice constraints. It does not prescribe a particular algebraic modeling language.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proposed homogenized feasible set \(M\subset\mathbb R\times X\times\mathbb R\) has missing homogenized domain constraints when it agrees with the perspective epigraph at positive scale but is not equal to the closed epigraph: \[M\cap\{t>0\}=E\cap\{t>0\},\qquad M\neq E.\] It is an outer domain omission when \(E\subsetneq M\), and an inner domain omission when \(M\subsetneq E\). The canonical domain conditions encoded by \(E\) are \(t\geq0\), \(r\geq t\varphi(x/t)\) for \(t>0\), and \(r\geq(\operatorname{rec}\varphi)(x)\) for \(t=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A homogenized model is domain-incomplete when it is correct at every positive scale but differs from the closed perspective epigraph somewhere else. If it contains extra points it is an outer omission; if it loses required points it is an inner omission. The complete model requires nonnegative scale, the perspective inequality at positive scale, and the recession inequality at zero scale.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The defect set is \(\Delta(M,E)=(M\setminus E)\cup(E\setminus M)\), and domain completeness is equivalent to \(\Delta(M,E)=\varnothing\).
An outer omission admits at least one spurious point in \(M\setminus E\); an inner omission excludes at least one valid point in \(E\setminus M\).
special_cases_latex: Omitting \(t\geq0\) can admit negative-scale points if the remaining algebraic constraints do not exclude them.
Using only \((t,x)=(0,0)\) at zero scale is an inner omission whenever \(\operatorname{dom}(\operatorname{rec}\varphi)\neq\{0\}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Agreement on \(t=1\) or even on all \(t>0\) does not establish equality of closed homogenized models.
An outer omission may weaken an optimization problem; an inner omission may destroy closedness or attainment.
boundary_notes: A redundant omitted inequality is not a missing domain constraint because it does not change \(M\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lifted Representation of a Set or Function
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\) be an extended-space feasible set, and let \(\pi_x(x,u)=x\). For a function \(f\), apply the same construction to \(\operatorname{epi}f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is the abstract finite-dimensional projection interface. The internal set may be polyhedral, conic, semidefinite, or another closed convex representable set; cone catalogs and solver consequences are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A lifted representation interface for \(X\) is a pair \((Q,\pi_x)\) satisfying \[X=\pi_x(Q)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists u\in\mathbb R^m\text{ with }(x,u)\in Q\}.\] It is exact when equality holds and outer-relaxed when only \(X\subseteq\pi_x(Q)\) holds. A lifted representation of an extended-real function \(f\) is a set \(Q_f\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^m\) such that \[\operatorname{epi}f=\{(x,t):\exists u\ (x,t,u)\in Q_f\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted representation introduces auxiliary variables and a feasible set in the enlarged variable space. The target set consists exactly of the original-variable components that possess at least one feasible auxiliary completion. For a function, the represented object is its epigraph. Equality gives an exact lift; one-sided containment gives an outer relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x\in X\iff\exists u\in\mathbb R^m:(x,u)\in Q,\qquad (x,t)\in\operatorname{epi}f\iff\exists u:(x,t,u)\in Q_f.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The indicator satisfies \(\iota_X(x)=\inf_{u\in\mathbb R^m}\iota_Q(x,u)\).
A function lift may be written \(f(x)=\inf\{t:\exists u\ (x,t,u)\in Q_f\}\), provided the epigraph identity is exact.
special_cases_latex: If \(m=0\), the lift is the original formulation.
If \(Q=\{(x,u):A x+B u-b\in K\}\), the interface is a conic lift.
If \(Q\) is an affine slice of a positive-semidefinite cone, its projection is a semidefinite representation.
immediate_consequences_latex: Membership in the target is an existential feasibility statement over auxiliary variables.
Different extended sets can represent the same target after projection.
boundary_notes: Projection need not preserve closedness, even when \(Q\) is closed and convex.
Exactness does not imply a small or computationally useful lift.
This interface does not include extension-complexity lower bounds or solver selection.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) be a convex cone, \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\) and \(B:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^q\) be linear, and \(b\in\mathbb R^q\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition captures the common structural architecture of lifted convex representations: an affine inverse image of a cone followed by coordinate projection. It does not classify particular cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cone-based lift architecture is the tuple \(\mathfrak L=(K,A,B,b,\pi_x)\) with lifted feasible set \[Q_{\mathfrak L}=\{(x,u)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m:A x+B u-b\in K\}\] and represented set \[X_{\mathfrak L}=\pi_x(Q_{\mathfrak L})=\{x:\exists u,\ A x+B u-b\in K\}.\] Two architectures are representation-equivalent when their represented sets coincide, even if their auxiliary dimensions, cones, or affine maps differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lift architecture consists of a cone, affine data linking original and auxiliary variables, and projection back to the original variables. Its lifted feasible set is the affine inverse image of the cone, and its represented set is the coordinate projection of that feasible set. Architectures with different internal data are representation-equivalent when they project to the same target set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathfrak L=(K,A,B,b,\pi_x),\quad Q_{\mathfrak L}=\{(x,u):Ax+Bu-b\in K\},\quad X_{\mathfrak L}=\pi_x(Q_{\mathfrak L}).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Membership has the quantified form \(x\in X_{\mathfrak L}\iff\exists u\; Ax+Bu-b\in K\).
Writing \(L(x,u)=Ax+Bu-b\), one has \(Q_{\mathfrak L}=L^{-1}(K)\) and \(X_{\mathfrak L}=\pi_x(L^{-1}(K))\).
special_cases_latex: For \(K=\mathbb R_+^q\), the architecture is a polyhedral extended formulation.
For \(K\) a product of second-order cones, it is a conic-quadratic architecture.
For \(K\) a positive-semidefinite cone and an affine symmetric-matrix map, it is a semidefinite architecture.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(K\) is convex, then both \(Q_{\mathfrak L}\) and \(X_{\mathfrak L}\) are convex.
An invertible affine change of auxiliary coordinates preserves the represented set after the corresponding change to \(B\) and \(b\).
boundary_notes: Closedness of \(K\) and \(Q_{\mathfrak L}\) does not by itself ensure closedness of \(X_{\mathfrak L}\).
Representation equivalence does not assert equal lift size or equal computational behavior.
Nonconic extended formulations require a broader architecture than the tuple defined here.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^{n+m}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), define \(f:\mathbb R^n\to[-\infty,+\infty]\) by \(f(x)=\inf_{z\in\mathbb R^m}F(x,z)\), and let \(P(x,z,r)=(x,r)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This finite-dimensional definition allows unattained infima. It separates the projected epigraph from its closure and therefore records the exactness boundary of the lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The epigraph-partial-minimization lift generated by \(F\) is \[Q_F:=\operatorname{epi}F=\{(x,z,r):F(x,z)\leq r\},\qquad f(x):=\inf_zF(x,z).\] Its projected epigraph satisfies \[P(Q_F)\subseteq\operatorname{epi}f\subseteq\operatorname{cl}P(Q_F).\] The lift is epigraph-exact when \(P(Q_F)=\operatorname{epi}f\); equivalently, for every \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), the infimum defining \(f(x)\) is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a function of original and auxiliary variables, partially minimize over the auxiliary variable. The epigraph of the original function is the lifted set. Its projection is always contained in the epigraph of the marginal function, while the marginal epigraph is contained in the closure of that projection. Equality with the projection is the exact regime and corresponds to attainment of every finite partial infimum.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A point \((x,r)\) belongs to \(P(\operatorname{epi}F)\) exactly when some \(z\) satisfies \(F(x,z)\leq r\).
At a finite marginal value, \((x,f(x))\in P(\operatorname{epi}F)\) exactly when \(\operatorname{argmin}_zF(x,z)\neq\varnothing\).
special_cases_latex: If \(F\) is convex, then \(f\) is convex.
If \(F\) is closed proper convex and an auxiliary-variable level set is nonempty and compact under the cited criterion, then \(f\) is closed proper convex and all finite partial minima are attained.
immediate_consequences_latex: A failure of attainment can remove lower-boundary points from the projected epigraph without changing its closure.
Closedness of \(\operatorname{epi}F\) alone is insufficient to guarantee epigraph exactness after projection.
boundary_notes: The marginal function may take \(-\infty\) unless additional properness assumptions are imposed.
The equality criterion concerns all finite marginal values, not merely equality of optimal values in one optimization problem.
Infinite-dimensional analogues require additional topological qualifications.

knowledge_statements.title: Epigraph Lifts
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An epigraph lift places retained and auxiliary variables in a jointly convex epigraph. Its projection lies in the marginal epigraph and equals it exactly when every finite marginal value is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An epigraph lift of the marginal \(g\) is the convex set \[L=\operatorname{epi}F=\bigl\{(x,y,r)\in X\times Y\times\mathbb R:F(x,y)\le r\bigr\},\] in which \(y\) is auxiliary and \(g(x)=\inf_{y\in Y}F(x,y)\). Its projection is \[\pi_{X\times\mathbb R}(L)=\bigl\{(x,r)\in X\times\mathbb R:\text{there exists }y\in Y\text{ with }F(x,y)\le r\bigr\}\subseteq\operatorname{epi}g.\] Equality holds if and only if, for every \(x\in X\) with \(g(x)\in\mathbb R\), there exists \(y\in Y\) such that \(F(x,y)=g(x)\).
assumptions_latex: The marginal \(g(x)=\inf_{y\in Y}F(x,y)\) satisfies \(g(x)>-\infty\) for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projection of \(\operatorname{epi}F\) is contained in \(\operatorname{epi}g\), with equality exactly when every finite marginal value is attained.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph lift with auxiliary variables in finite dimensions and an explicit marginal interface.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Minimization Lifts
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial minimization of a jointly convex function is convex, and under attainment its epigraph equals the projection of the lifted epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the partial-minimization lift by \[g(x)=\inf_{y\in Y}F(x,y).\] Then \(g\) is convex, possibly extended-valued, and attainment yields the exact identity \[\operatorname{epi}g=\bigl\{(x,r)\in X\times\mathbb R:\text{there exists }y\in Y\text{ such that }F(x,y)\le r\bigr\}=\pi_{X\times\mathbb R}(\operatorname{epi}F).\] Without attainment, the displayed projection can omit boundary points at height \(g(x)\).
assumptions_latex: \(F(x,\cdot)\) has a minimizer whenever its infimum is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The marginal \(g\) is convex and its epigraph is the projection of \(\operatorname{epi}F\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact marginal representation under pointwise attainment.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain projection and the unbounded-below fiber obstruction to a proper marginal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:X\times Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex and define \(g(x)=\inf_{y\in Y}F(x,y)\). If \(g(x)>-\infty\) for every \(x\), then
\[
\operatorname{dom}g=\pi_X(\operatorname{dom}F),
\]
and \(g\) is proper and convex. Joint properness alone is insufficient: if \(F(x,y)=y\) on \(X\times\mathbb R\), then \(F\) is proper, closed, and affine, but \(g(x)=-\infty\) for every \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absent fibers unbounded below, the marginal is proper and its domain is the projection of the joint domain; joint properness alone does not prevent a marginal equal to minus infinity.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are finite-dimensional real vector spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(g(x)>-\infty\) for all \(x\), then \(\operatorname{dom}g=\pi_X(\operatorname{dom}F)\) and \(g\) is proper; an unbounded-below fiber can destroy properness.

notation.meaning: partial minimum of \(F\) over the auxiliary variable

knowledge_statements.title: Properness Boundary for Partial Minimization
Exact Strict-Epigraph Projection
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projected lifted epigraph always contains the strict epigraph of the marginal; only unattained boundary points can be absent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:X\times Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), let \(g(x)=\inf_{y\in Y}F(x,y)\), and suppose \(g(x)>-\infty\) for every \(x\). Then \[\{(x,r):g(x)<r\}\subseteq\pi_{X\times\mathbb R}(\operatorname{epi}F)\subseteq\operatorname{epi}g.\] Hence the projection can omit only a boundary point \((x,g(x))\), and that point belongs to the projection exactly when the infimum defining \(g(x)\) is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}_{<}g\subseteq\pi_{X\times\mathbb R}(\operatorname{epi}F)\subseteq\operatorname{epi}g\), with boundary membership equivalent to attainment.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment-free part of the epigraphical projection interface.

knowledge_statements.title: Epigraphical Projection Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projected lifted epigraph may miss unattained boundary points; attainment gives exact projection, while lower semicontinuity identifies the marginal epigraph with its closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[P=\pi_{X\times\mathbb R}(\operatorname{epi}F).\] Then \[P\subseteq\operatorname{epi}g\subseteq\operatorname{cl}P.\] The first inclusion follows from the definition of the infimum, while the second records approximation by auxiliary points with values arbitrarily close to \(g(x)\). Moreover, \(P=\operatorname{epi}g\) exactly when every finite marginal value is attained. If \(g\) is lower semicontinuous, then \(\operatorname{epi}g=\operatorname{cl}P\).
assumptions_latex: \(F:X\times Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and convex on finite-dimensional spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Projection lies between the marginal epigraph and its closure, with exactness under attainment.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and closure-level interfaces between epigraph projection and marginalization.

knowledge_statements.title: Elimination Closure Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projected epigraph is closed precisely when the marginal is lower semicontinuous and all finite marginal values are attained; without attainment, closure recovers the marginal epigraph when the marginal is lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[P=\pi_{X\times\mathbb R}(\operatorname{epi}F).\] The following conditions are equivalent: \(P\) is closed; \(g\) is lower semicontinuous and, for every \(x\in X\) with \(g(x)\in\mathbb R\), there exists \(y\in Y\) such that \(F(x,y)=g(x)\); and \[P=\operatorname{epi}g\quad\text{with}\quad\operatorname{epi}g\text{ closed}.\] If attainment fails while \(g\) remains lower semicontinuous, then \[\operatorname{cl}P=\operatorname{epi}g.\]
assumptions_latex: \(F:X\times Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The marginal \(g(x)=\inf_{y\in Y}F(x,y)\) satisfies \(g(x)>-\infty\) for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projected epigraph is closed exactly when elimination yields the closed marginal epigraph; equivalently, \(g\) is lower semicontinuous and every finite marginal value is attained.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent closedness conditions for eliminating auxiliary variables.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) be convex, let \(L:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^q\) be linear, let \(c\in\mathbb R^q\), and let \(\pi_x(x,u)=x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This finite-dimensional correspondence identifies existential affine constraints with projection of an affine inverse image. It includes conic and semidefinite slices but makes no cone-specific duality claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The affine-slice lift determined by \((C,L,c)\) is \[Q:=\{(x,u):L(x,u)-c\in C\}=L_c^{-1}(C),\qquad L_c(x,u)=L(x,u)-c.\] Its projection is \[X:=\pi_x(Q)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists u\in\mathbb R^m,\ L(x,u)-c\in C\}.\] The affine-slice projection-lift correspondence is the equivalence \[x\in X\iff\exists u\;(x,u)\in Q\iff\exists u\;L(x,u)-c\in C.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Take an affine inverse image of a convex set in a space containing original and auxiliary variables, then project away the auxiliary variables. Membership in the projected set is equivalent to the existence of an auxiliary completion satisfying the affine-slice constraint. This is the affine-slice projection-lift correspondence.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(L(x,u)=Ax+Bu\), then \(X=\{x:\exists u,\ Ax+Bu-c\in C\}\).
The indicator identity is \(\iota_X(x)=\inf_u\iota_C(L(x,u)-c)\).
special_cases_latex: For \(C=\{0\}\), the lift consists of affine equality constraints.
For \(C=K\) a convex cone, this is a conic lift.
For \(C=\mathbb S_+^k\) and symmetric-matrix-valued \(L_c\), the construction is a semidefinite representation.
immediate_consequences_latex: Convexity of \(C\) implies convexity of both \(Q\) and \(X\).
Multiple auxiliary witnesses may correspond to the same projected point.
boundary_notes: A linear image of a closed convex set need not be closed when the set is unbounded.
The word slice includes affine inverse images, not only intersections with coordinate hyperplanes.
The correspondence asserts set equality and does not assert preservation of facial structure.

notation.meaning: affine map obtained from L by subtracting c

knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Slice Lifts
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine-slice lift intersects a lifted convex set with affine equations and projects away auxiliary variables to represent a convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(b\in Z\), an affine-slice lift represents \(C\subseteq X\) by \[C=\bigl\{x\in X:\text{there exists }y\in Y\text{ such that }(x,y)\in K\text{ and }Ax+By=b\bigr\}.\] Equivalently, \[C=\pi_X\bigl(K\cap\{(x,y):Ax+By=b\}\bigr).\] The sliced lift is convex, so its projection \(C\) is convex, although it need not be closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The represented set is the projection of a convex set cut out by an affine slice.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional affine-slice extended formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Lifts
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projection lift represents a set as the coordinate image of a higher-dimensional convex set; convexity survives projection, but closedness may not.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A projection lift of \(C\subseteq X\) is a convex set \(L\subseteq X\times Y\) satisfying \[C=\pi_X(L)=\bigl\{x\in X:\text{there exists }y\in Y\text{ with }(x,y)\in L\bigr\}.\] Because linear images of convex sets are convex, \(C\) is convex. Even when \(L\) is closed, \(C\) may fail to be closed, so closed representability requires an additional image-closedness condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C=\pi_X(L)\) is convex, but closedness need not pass from \(L\) to \(C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-projection formulation of convex lifts.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support Identity and Visible Separation Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-function and strict nonmembership interface for a convex projection lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\subseteq X\times Y\) be nonempty and convex and let \(C=\pi_X(L)\). For every \(u\in X^*\), \[\sigma_C(u)=\sigma_L(u,0).\] Moreover, for \(\bar x\in X\), \[\bar x\notin\operatorname{cl}C\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists u\in X^*:\ \langle u,\bar x\rangle>\sigma_L(u,0).\] Thus a strict visible-space separator is precisely a lifted separator with zero auxiliary dual component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The support function of a projection is the lifted support function at zero auxiliary dual coordinate, yielding exact strict certificates outside the projected closure.
assumptions_latex: \(L\subseteq X\times Y\) is nonempty and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_C(u)=\sigma_L(u,0)\), and \(\bar x\notin\operatorname{cl}C\) exactly when some \(u\) satisfies \(\langle u,\bar x\rangle>\sigma_L(u,0)\).

notation.meaning: Support function of the projected set
Support function of the lifted set
Lifted dual functional with zero auxiliary component

knowledge_statements.title: Support Identity and Visible Separation Certificates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transitivity of existential auxiliary-variable representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq X\times Y\times Z\), set \(L=\pi_{X\times Y}(Q)\), and set \(C=\pi_X(L)\). Then \[C=\pi_X(Q)=\{x:\exists y\in Y,\exists z\in Z\text{ such that }(x,y,z)\in Q\}.\] Hence projection lifts compose, and convexity of \(Q\) implies convexity of both \(L\) and \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested projection lifts flatten into one projection by retaining all auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_X(\pi_{X\times Y}(Q))=\pi_X(Q)\); if \(Q\) is convex, its intermediate and final projections are convex.
knowledge_statements.title: Composition of Projection Lifts
Slice–Projection Correspondence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine-slice lifts are projection lifts of constrained convex sets, while ordinary projection lifts arise by using a vacuous affine slice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The affine-slice representation \[C=\pi_X\bigl(K\cap M^{-1}(b)\bigr)\] is a projection lift with lifted set \(L=K\cap M^{-1}(b)\). Conversely, any projection lift \(C=\pi_X(L)\) is an affine-slice lift by taking \(K=L\), the zero map \(M=0\), and \(b=0\). Thus the two architectures differ only in whether affine constraints are displayed separately from the lifted convex set.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq X\times Y\) is convex in finite dimensions.
\(M:X\times Y\to Z\) is linear and \(b\in Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every affine-slice lift is a projection lift, and every projection lift is the trivial-slice case.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence of slicing-plus-projection and projection of a constrained lift.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonclosed Image Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex epigraph can have a nonclosed coordinate projection, so closed lifted sets do not automatically yield closed represented sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The set \[L=\bigl\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x>0,\ y\ge1/x\bigr\}\] is the epigraph of the convex function \(x\mapsto1/x\) on \((0,+\infty)\), extended by \(+\infty\) elsewhere; hence \(L\) is closed and convex. Nevertheless, \[\pi_x(L)=(0,+\infty),\] which is not closed. Indeed, \(1/n\in\pi_x(L)\) converges to \(0\notin\pi_x(L)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\) is closed and convex, but \(\pi_x(L)=(0,+\infty)\) is not closed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard finite-dimensional example of a nonclosed projection.
